newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher in active trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended higher in active trading that brokers said was fueled by continuing demand for brewer Bavaria and Compania Suramericana de Seguros of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index ended up 0.46 percent at 17,191.78 on above-average trading volume of nearly 4.8 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB closed up 0.70 percent, meanwhile, ending the day at 1,130.15 on volume of more than 3.6 billion pesos.
"It was expected that after last week's slip Bavaria, would start being demanded again, especially by the foreign funds," one Bogota-based broker said.

Bavaria, flagship of the Julio Mario Santo Domingo industrial group, has risen more than 20 percent in nominal terms since April 1 on rumors that Brazil's Companhia Cervejaria Brahma was considering buying a stake in the company.
It gave up some of its gains Thursday and Friday but closed up 1.71 percent Monday at 8,047 pesos per share.
Suramericana de Seguros, the country's leading insurer, ended up 1.58 percent at 25,700 pesos per share on what brokers described as renewed foreign buying in the firm.
Winners included blue-chip Banco Ganadero, whose ordinary stock rose 0.83 percent to end at 361 pesos per share.

Banco de Colombia, the country's second largest bank after Ganadero, gave up 0.47 percent to close down at 421 pesos per share, however, on what brokers described as investor concerns about delays in its long-awaited strategic alliance with Spain's Banco Central Hispano.
